identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Badrinath is one of the four Char Dham shrines and one of the 108 Divya Desams, dedicated to Vishnu as Badrinarayan. The image in the sanctum is a black stone figure about a foot high, seated in meditation and holding a conch and discus. Unusually for a north Indian temple, the head priest — the Rawal — is drawn from Kerala's Nambudiri Brahmin community, a practice tradition attributes to Adi Shankara.

narrative.summaryIntro:
Badrinath Temple is one of the four cardinal shrines (Char Dham) of Hindu pilgrimage and is dedicated to Lord Vishnu in his form as Badrinath (Badrinarayan). Located in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand at an elevation of 3,300 meters, the temple is situated in a scenic valley surrounded by the Himalayas.

The temple features a distinctive red and gold pagoda-style architecture. It has been a major pilgrimage center for centuries, attracting devotees from across India and the world who seek blessings and spiritual enlightenment at this sacred shrine of Vishnu.
narrative.documentedHistory:
The temple stands at roughly 3,100 m on the bank of the Alaknanda in the Garhwal Himalaya. It is counted both among the four Char Dham shrines and among the 108 Divya Desams of the Vaishnava canon. The deity is a black stone image of Vishnu as Badrinarayan, about a foot high, seated in a meditative posture and holding a conch and a discus. Adjacent to the temple is the Tapt Kund, a hot spring that runs at a near-constant temperature and in which pilgrims bathe before darshan.

The priesthood is distinctive: the head priest, titled Rawal, is traditionally a Nambudiri Brahmin from Kerala, a practice attributed to Adi Shankara and unusual for a temple in north India.

The shrine is administered by the Shri Badarinath Kedarnath Temple Committee, a state-appointed body of seventeen members constituted under a 1939 Act, which also administers Kedarnath. The committee runs the online booking system for pujas, paths, aartis and bhog, and prior registration is mandatory for them.

visitingInfo.dressCode: Warm clothing essential; traditional attire recommended
visitingInfo.entryRules: Prior registration is mandatory before booking any puja, path, aarti or bhog, and pilgrim registration is done through the Uttarakhand government portal registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in. Anyone attending a booked puja must carry a valid government photo ID — voter ID, Aadhaar, driving licence, passport or PAN card — along with the booking receipt, and should reach the temple gate 15 to 30 minutes before the slot. Booking and donation amounts are non-refundable and non-transferable to another name or date.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Badrinath is a seasonal shrine and the kapat opening and closing dates are announced afresh each year — do not plan on fixed dates. Confirm the current season's dates, darshan hours and road status with BKTC on 0135-2741600 or the Badarinath pilgrims helpline +91-8979001008 (support Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 5 pm) before travelling.

openingHours.notes: Badrinath is open for roughly six months a year, from late April to early November; it is closed through the winter because of snow and the deity's worship moves to the Narasimha temple at Jyotirmath (Joshimath). The exact kapat opening and closing dates are fixed and announced annually and differ every year — no fixed dates are recorded here. The BKTC portal does not publish daily darshan hours, so none are recorded either.
